html:
Santo Domingo was the Spanish colony on the island of Hispaniola, in the eastern part that is now the Dominican Republic. The map shows it in 1715.

It was Spain's first colony in the Americas, begun after Columbus reached the Caribbean, and its capital, Santo Domingo, held the first cathedral, university and royal court in the New World. Spanish rule and disease destroyed the Taíno within a few decades. Once Mexico and Peru were conquered, settlers left, and the colony became a poor land of cattle ranches.

French buccaneers settled the empty west of the island, and in the Peace of Ryswick of 1697 Spain accepted that the west belonged to France. It became Saint-Domingue, the richest sugar colony in the world, while Spanish Santo Domingo stayed thinly settled. In 1795 Spain gave its part of the island to France too. See also Hispaniola and Haiti on the map.
sum: Santo Domingo was the Spanish colony on the island of Hispaniola, in the eastern part that is now the Dominican Republic. The map shows it in 1715.
